payload.summary: The three-stage delivery shape is sensible, but the proposal is not yet a complete executable hierarchy and cannot be affirmed against the approved GoalExecutionProposal. The durable execution proposal authorizes only Issue 60 and has empty capabilities, issues, dependencies, repositories, validations, reviewers, risks, irreversible actions, product outcome, and duration/token estimates; Issue 60 does not materialize the proposed dependency hierarchy. Repository evidence also contradicts key assumptions and leaves release/deployment acceptance unverifiable: the named consolidation branch has no commits beyond main, numerous other remote branches do, the release workflow is mutable, and no canonical production target or rollback procedure is identified.

findings.title: Reviewed breakdown is not represented by the approved execution proposal
findings.evidence: bos_get_goal_execution returns capabilities=[], issues=[], dependencies=[], repositories=[], requiredValidations=[], requiredReviewers=[], riskTags=[], irreversibleActions=[], productOutcome=null, proposalVersion=null, while approval refers to proposalVersion 1. Only Issue 60 is included. Issue 60 has no dependencies and its four broad criteria do not encode the breakdown's five proposed Issues or three capability gates.
findings.request: Produce a versioned GoalExecutionProposal whose included executable hierarchy, dependencies, repository, validations/reviews, irreversible boundaries, outcome, and budgets/duration match the reviewed breakdown, or simplify the breakdown explicitly to one Issue with an equally complete staged checklist and durable artifacts. Do not rely on prose in an unapproved planning record as inherited execution authorization.

findings.title: History inventory is unbounded and its starting assumption is contradicted by repository state
findings.evidence: At review time origin/codex/goal-216-consolidate-symphony is 3 commits behind origin/main and 0 ahead; origin/codex/release-symphony-consolidated likewise exposes no unique candidate commits in the inspected clone. Conversely, dozens of other origin branches are ahead of main by 1-9 commits. Issue 60 asserts that the integration branch already preserves substantive worktree histories, but neither it nor the proposal names a ledger artifact, discovery roots, remote snapshot, cutoff, or exact candidate ref proving that assertion.
findings.request: Define the finite inventory universe and cutoff (clone/worktree roots, refs, remote snapshot timestamp), the durable ledger location/schema, and an objective disposition rule. Remove the unsupported precondition that consolidation is already complete, and make candidate identity an output of inventory/integration rather than an assumed branch.

findings.title: Immutable release acceptance conflicts with the canonical workflow and omits version-bump ordering
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/burrito-release.yml uses `gh release upload ... --clobber` for an existing tag, so the current canonical workflow permits asset mutation. It also requires the tag to equal elixir/mix.exs version. The repository is currently version 0.2.1 and immutable tag v0.2.1 already exists. The proposal says derive a new SemVer after merge, but changing mix.exs after candidate validation changes the exact commit and invalidates the evidence/merged-SHA identity.
findings.request: Specify the unused next SemVer and include the version bump in the candidate before exact-SHA validation and merge. Either change the workflow within approved scope to fail closed when a release/tag exists and never clobber assets, or weaken/redefine immutability with an explicit accepted compatibility contract; the current proposal may not claim both.

findings.title: Production target, deployment operation, verification oracle, and rollback path are undefined
findings.evidence: .bos/project.yaml declares production policy flags but no provider target, server/project identifier, URL, health/version endpoint, runtime identity probe, or rollback reference. The repository exposes a Burrito GitHub release workflow, which builds downloadable binaries but does not identify a canonical continuously running production runtime. The breakdown nevertheless requires provider, version, health, logs, runtime, functional, security-boundary, browser, and verified rollback checks.
findings.request: Name the canonical production target and governed operation, exact identity oracle, required probe inputs and pass/fail thresholds, and a reversible rollback reference/procedure. If the product's canonical production outcome is only a GitHub release artifact, remove daemon/browser/server deployment claims and define artifact installation/smoke verification instead. Ensure any rollback boundary is present in the approved execution contract.

findings.title: Several gates are conditional, duplicated, or not objectively decidable
findings.evidence: The proposal alternates between browser verification when a browser surface is present and visual review only when UI changed, without a deterministic applicability decision. `complete available QA`, `where available`, `required runtime/browser verification`, `no leaked child processes`, and `security-boundary checks` do not name commands, environments, scanners, process-scan method, or artifacts. The project requires `cd elixir && mise exec -- mix test`; nearby instructions require `make all` and `mix specs.check`, while make all already runs coverage tests, creating acknowledged but unexplained duplicate execution.
findings.request: Replace open-ended gates with an applicability matrix and exact commands/artifacts. State who/what decides UI/browser applicability, define the child-process baseline and scan, enumerate security/architecture review outputs, and order checks so inexpensive targeted/spec checks precede full make all while still satisfying the repository-required command.

findings.title: One delivery Issue is asked to stand in for five proposed Issues without executable handoffs
findings.evidence: The planning record proposes inventory -> integration -> assurance -> merge/release/deploy as separate dependent work, but says existing Issue 60 can materialize it. Issue 60 combines candidate verification, PR/merge, release, and production verification, omits inventory/integration scope and dependency artifacts, and is currently agent:blocked with an active claim. This loses the clean handoffs the proposal cites as its rationale.
findings.request: Choose one coherent model: materialize the staged hierarchy with explicit artifact/SHA handoffs, or keep Issue 60 and collapse the planning hierarchy into a single executable sequence containing those same gates. Avoid maintaining both a detailed non-executable shadow plan and a broad executable Issue.
